speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) whether the Ministry will introduce mandatory, centralised government security vetting for personnel with access to Singapore’s critical information infrastructure to mitigate insider threats; and (b) if not, how the Ministry ensures that current employer-led vetting of personnel, including foreign nationals, in sensitive technical roles is sufficiently robust against sophisticated state-sponsored cyber threats.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government takes the cybersecurity of our CIIs very seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to review the standards we require and consider further enhancements that could be effective.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am asking more in terms of dealing with the issue upstream, in terms of vetting personnel.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And given that many technical experts in our telco and energy sectors are foreign nationals, what specific assistance does the Cyber Security Agency provide to private CII owners to verify the backgrounds of such individuals?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And could the Ministry introduce a tiered vetting system, where personnel with super user or administrator access rights to our sensitive core areas of our CII must undergo Government-led G50 security clearance, just like public servants and vendors who access our Government systems?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is the first point I want to put across.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You do not want to have a preconceived idea that this profile would necessarily be safer than another profile.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, we also do not assume that security vetting is a silver bullet.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If a nefarious actor is determined to infiltrate the system and they know that there is a vetting process of some sort, then clearly, it would be an effort on their part to overcome whatever it is that would stand in the way of them clearing a vetting system.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, a vetting system is also not a silver bullet.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And you are very careful about who you provide more access to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is the approach that we take, rather than to think that just because we have done security vetting upstream, other controls are not as important; or since they have cleared vetting, then it is safe.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not make that sort of assumption.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Security by design means that you have all these multiple layers of defences in order to be able to guard against the cyber risk.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I agree that we should not assume any of these things and we should not assume that just because someone is security cleared, therefore they are safe to continue using the systems.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But in this age of cybersecurity threats and Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs), should we not consider that aligning the security clearance of our CII personnel, especially those with access to sensitive systems, with public servants?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Because our all public servants have to go through this standard security vetting.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Why not we extend that to CII personnel as well?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we do not publicly reveal all the requirements that we put in place, and that is for obvious security reasons.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because if it was so plain, if you state it so clearly that there is this particular process and once you clear it, that is it.
